thread:
sam-runtime: quick heads-up — ran an Nsight GPU trace on the 8-card DP+TP run during a batch-size sweep. with KV cache enabled we see periodic all-reduce tails (~6-12 ms) that line up with cache refill windows. ping @jia-ml @lena-sre

jia-ml: can you paste the capture id and timeline link?

sam-runtime: perf-bot uploaded: https://perf.captures/1859876543.trace (tag: bs-sweep-kv-on) :eyes:

mike-eng: quick q — are we using fused all-reduce or the default NCCL ring? also kernel selection mode?

sam-runtime: default nccl ring with tensor-parallel sync. kernel selection used fabric-opt (auto). config snippet:
```
TP=2
PP=1
BATCHES=[1,2,4,8]
KV_CACHE=on
KERNEL_PATH=auto
```

lena-sre: timeline shows repeated stalls on rank1 around step boundaries — looks like uneven prefetch across ranks. any per-rank op counts or memcpy spikes?

sam-runtime: attached per-rank timers in the capture. rank1 shows an extra memcpy right before the all-reduce kickoff, probably due to KV cache population hitting a slow-kernel fallback on that card.

jia-ml: hypothesis: kernel selector picks different codegen on some ranks (quantized vs FP) causing reorder/extra work. can you grep for 'fallback' in the runtime stdout in the capture?

sam-runtime: grepped: "kernel_fallback: conv-attn-kqv -> scalar-quant-fallback" appears on rank1 and rank3 intermittently.

mike-eng: that mismatch would desync comm/compute timings and explain waiting on all-reduce. try forcing KERNEL_PATH=compat to make the kernel selection deterministic across ranks.

sam-runtime: ran with KERNEL_PATH=compat, new capture: https://perf.captures/1859877001.trace — tails shrink to ~1-3 ms but overall step latency is +4% (slower kernels). tradeoff as expected.

lena-sre: can we stagger KV prefetch across ranks so not all ranks start population at same time? saw simultaneous memcopies causing IO contention. quick patch idea:
```
kv_prefetch_offset = rank_id % stagger_window
start_prefetch_at(step + kv_prefetch_offset)
```

jia-ml: also compute the all-reduce overlap metric: allreduce_wait_time / step_time. what's that ratio in the original trace vs compat?

sam-runtime: original (auto): avg allreduce_wait_time / step_time = 0.28. compat run -> 0.12. if stagger prefetch works we expect ~0.08 or lower.

mike-eng: other quick test: disable prefetch entirely and re-run bs=8 to see if batching masks the refill. if tails disappear, then cache prefetch is main culprit.

sam-runtime: scheduled overnight runs: kv_prefetch=off, and kv_prefetch_stagger=2 for bs=1,4,8. I'll post the numbers tomorrow morning.

perf-bot: job 1859876543-rt queued -> running on perf-farm. ETA 6h.

jia-ml: perfect, thanks. if stagger reduces the peaks we should wire an automated heuristic: if per-rank memcpy variance > X then enable staggered prefetch and/or fallback to unified kernel path.

sam-runtime: opening GH issue with capture links, raw timers, and initial triage notes. adding checklist of experiments. :memo:

mike-eng: next steps (concise):
1) repro auto vs compat across bs=1,4,8 (capture both)
2) run with kv_prefetch=off (bs=8)
3) run with stagger window 2 and 4 (bs=1,4)
4) collect per-rank memcpy hist and allreduce_wait ratio, post csv

sam-runtime: adding checklist to issue and will attach captures + per-rank stats when runs complete. :thumbsup:
